report.heading: Your wellness plan
report.intro: Based on your answers, your body needs extra support in 7 key areas. Your full plan is below, with the breakdown at the end.

products.name: Core Vitamin B12
products.why: Your answers suggest your vitamin B12 intake is below your target, and it matches your boost energy goal.
products.description: Found almost nowhere outside animal foods, which is why it is the supplement most vegans take first. Methylcobalamin is the form the body uses directly. Vitamin B12 contributes to the reduction of tiredness and fatigue and to normal red blood cell formation.

products.name: Focus Quercetin Complex
products.why: It matches your plant-based nutrition goal. This one is a plant extract.
products.description: A plant pigment found in onion skin, capers and apple peel, paired here with the vitamin C it is usually taken alongside.

products.name: Peak Creatine Complex
products.description: Stored in muscle and supplied in small amounts by red meat and fish. Monohydrate is the form nearly every study has used. Creatine increases physical performance in successive bursts of short-term, high-intensity exercise. The beneficial effect is obtained with a daily intake of 3g of creatine.

products.name: Flora Probiotic Complex
products.why: It matches your plant-based nutrition goal. This one is a digestive support.
products.description: Lactobacillus acidophilus with cranberry and B6, aimed at the urinary tract rather than the gut alone.

products.name: Calm Chamomile Extract
products.why: You told us about trouble falling asleep and trouble winding down.
products.description: The flower behind the evening tea, concentrated into a capsule so there is nothing to brew.

products.name: Calm Valerian Root
products.why: You told us about trouble falling asleep and racing mind at bedtime. This one is a herbal extract.
products.description: A root from European herbal tradition, and one with a famously strong smell.

products.name: Calm L-Theanine
products.why: You told us about trouble falling asleep and racing mind at bedtime. This one is an amino acid.
products.description: An amino acid found in green tea leaves, taken in the evening rather than with a morning brew.

report.macros_note: Your intake is estimated from your height, weight, age and activity, then adjusted for your portion sizes and how often you skip meals. It is an estimate of a typical day, not a record of what you ate.

rows.name: Vitamin D3
rows.sources: Sources: eggs, vitamin-D-fortified foods and UV-exposed mushrooms. Food alone rarely covers vitamin D, particularly in winter.

rows.name: Iron
rows.sources: Sources: lentils, eggs and iron-fortified cereals.

rows.name: Selenium
rows.sources: Sources: eggs and Brazil nuts. Selenium content varies more than tenfold with where the nuts were grown, so no fixed number reliably covers a day, and more than three or four is too many.
